sections.title: 1. What is centralized logging?
sections.body:
(Essential for microservices)

Centralized logging means collecting logs from multiple services and storing them in a common logging platform.

Imagine your application has:

```text
FastAPI Service
Agent Service
RAG Service
LLM Gateway
Tool Service
Database Service
```

Each service generates logs.

Without centralized logging, you may need to access every server or container separately.

With centralized logging, logs are collected in one place.

scenario.title: Scenario — Observability 9. Centralized Logging and Log Aggregation
scenario.situation: Suppose your production application has five services. A user reports: "My research report is not generated." You open your centralized logging platform and search: text request_id = req-101 You find: text FastAPI: Request received Supervisor: Workflow started Research agent: Completed RAG service: Retrieved 5 chunks LLM gateway: Request timed out Report agent: Execution failed You can investigate the entire request

choices.label: Add detection signals first

choices.label: Apply a production fix / mitigation
choices.explanation: - Standardize JSON log formats. - Configure log collectors. - Monitor ingestion lag. - Use buffering and retry mechanisms. - Define retention periods. - Control storage costs. - Synchronize system clocks. - Restrict access to sensitive logs. **

sections.title: 4. Real-time AI application example
sections.body:
Suppose your production application has five services.

A user reports:

"My research report is not generated."

You open your centralized logging platform and search:

```text
request_id = req-101
```

You find:

```text
FastAPI:
Request received

Supervisor:
Workflow started

Research agent:
Completed

RAG service:
Retrieved 5 chunks

LLM gateway:
Request timed out

Report agent:
Execution failed
```

You can investigate the entire request without manually connecting to every service.

sections.title: 5. How to implement centralized logging?
sections.body:
A common production approach:

```text
Python application
      |
      v
Structured JSON logs
      |
      v
Container stdout/stderr
      |
      v
Fluent Bit / Collector
      |
      v
Elastic / Loki
      |
      v
Kibana / Grafana
```

In containerized applications, writing structured logs to standard output and standard error is a common pattern. A platform-level collector can then forward them to centralized storage.

sections.title: 6. How to detect centralized logging problems?
sections.body:
- Missing logs from a service.
- Log ingestion delays.
- Collector failures.
- Storage capacity exhaustion.
- Incorrect parsing.
- Duplicate ingestion.
- Logs arriving with incorrect timestamps.

sections.title: 7. How to fix them?
sections.body:
- Standardize JSON log formats.
- Configure log collectors.
- Monitor ingestion lag.
- Use buffering and retry mechanisms.
- Define retention periods.
- Control storage costs.
- Synchronize system clocks.
- Restrict access to sensitive logs.

**Interview question:** Why do we need centralized logging in microservices?

**Answer:** Because each microservice generates independent logs. Centralized logging combines those logs into one searchable platform, allowing engineers to investigate complete application behavior.

**Memory trick:** Local logs are scattered; centralized logging brings them together.
